hint.text:
The present perfect form is formed with the correct present tense form of the verb 'to have' and the past participle. For example: It has rained all day.

The past perfect form is formed with the correct past tense form of the verb 'to have' and the past participle. For example: It had rained all day yesterday.

instruction.text: Which sentences are in the perfect form?

atoms.b: Gemma had cooked dinner every evening this week.

instruction.text: Which sentences are in the perfect form?

atoms.b: Kyle has become a famous rock star.
He made a poster for his homework.

instruction.text: Select the verb phrases in the perfect form.

atoms.b: It ((has been)) three years since I started dance lessons. I ((have enjoyed)) learning to dance a lot and ((have made)) lots of new friends. Miss Jean ((has taught)) at the dance school for 25 years and she is the best teacher ever.
atoms.sound: It has been three years since I started dance lessons. I have enjoyed learning to dance a lot and have made lots of new friends. Miss Jean has taught at the dance school for 25 years and she is the best teacher ever.

instruction.text: Select the verb phrases in the perfect form.

atoms.b: Matty ((had been)) at the beach with his friends for a while. He played volleyball and then went in the sea for a bit. Matty’s mum ((had called)) him an hour ago telling him to come home, but he was having too much fun.
atoms.sound: Matty had been at the beach with his friends for a while. He played volleyball and then went in the sea for a bit. Matty’s mum had called him an hour ago telling him to come home, but he was having too much fun.

instruction.text: Is this sentence in the perfect form?

atoms.a: Nina has been a part of table tennis club for a year.
Henry had noticed that he had a headache during a work meeting.
Molly and Tom argued about which film to watch.
I have dark, curly hair but I want to dye it red.
